articles.title: Sepultura transfere show em estádio, em SP, para casa de show | G1
articles.standfirst: Apresentação do dia 7 de novembro passa de estádio com capacidade de mais de 40 mil pessoas para casa de shows com espaço para 9 mil. Motivo da mudança não foi divulgado.
articles.summary: Apresentação do dia 7 de novembro passa de estádio com capacidade de mais de 40 mil pessoas para casa de shows com espaço para 9 mil. Motivo da mudança não foi divulgado.
articles.body:
O Sepultura anunciou nesta terça-feira (8) a mudança do local de seu show em São Paulo em 7 de novembro. A apresentação, que aconteceria originalmente no Mercado Livre Arena Pacaembu, agora será realizada no Suhai Music Hall , na mesma data.

Com isso, o evento passa de um estádio com capacidade de mais de 40 mil pessoas para uma casa de shows com espaço para cerca de 9 mil fãs. O motivo da mudança não foi divulgado.

A organização afirma que os ingressos permanecem válidos para o novo local, mas quem quiser pode pedir um reembolso completo entre esta quinta (10) e o próximo dia 28 de setembro. Por ora, a apresentação tem entradas esgotadas.

Em sua turnê de despedida, o Sepultura realizou uma apresentação no Rock in Rio 2026 no último sábado (5), com um repertório dedicado à fase de Derrick Green como vocalista do grupo.

articles.title: LIV Golf files for US bankruptcy protection but reveals 2027 plans as players face uncertain future
articles.summary: LIV Golf released a statement on Tuesday regarding the league's future; Sky News understands LIV Golf is entering talks with players about whether they take part in the new iteration or elect to leave
articles.body:
On Tuesday the golf league announced it had entered into bankruptcy protection in an attempt to restructure after Saudi Arabia withdrew its financial backing.

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced earlier this year it would not bankroll the league beyond the 2026 campaign, having spent over $5bn (£3.6bn) over five years, leaving the circuit searching for fresh investment in recent months.

LIV Golf cut around 90 per cent of its staff after the conclusion of the season, as negotiations continued over its long-term future, with BC Partners later named as the proposed new investors.

Sky News understands LIV Golf is starting talks with players about whether they take part in the new iteration or elect to leave.

LIV Golf says a Chapter 11 petition has been filed to "preserve the company's business as a going concern through an innovative player-first ownership model".

In the statement on Tuesday, LIV Golf said the league is expected to be majority-owned by its players, with whom it "remains in advanced discussions".

LIV Golf chief executive Scott O'Neil said: "The people of LIV Golf, led by the players, have continued to show incredible resilience, commitment, and a shared belief in what we are building. Thanks to their tireless work, LIV Golf has created a foundation to entertain and inspire the next generation of global golf fans around the world.

"This process gives us the structure and time to pursue a landmark transaction and begin the next chapter of LIV Golf - one built around the fans, an innovative, player-first ownership model, and a part of the global golf ecosystem. We are excited about what lies ahead and yet, there is still much to accomplish in the months ahead.

"We believe deeply in LIV Golf's future, the opportunity in front of us, and the people who will help us realise it. We are grateful to our players, the incredible team at LIV Golf, our board, BC Partners, and our partners all over the world standing tall with us.

"We thank them for their belief in our next chapter. A special thank you to Ducera Partners who drove this investment process. We will not rest until we deliver on LIV Golf's full potential."

LIV Golf's Chapter 11 petition says the company ‌has between $500m (£370m) and $1bn (£730m) in liabilities, and between $100m (£74m) and $500m in assets.

The filing, made in the Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey, shows multiple LIV players as unsecured creditors, with at least $45m (£33m) still owed to players.

LIV said in its announcement that the PIF will provide an additional $49.6m (£36.6m) in financing, subject to court approval, while Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau were listed as the highest unsecured creditors on the bankruptcy document.

LIV Golf's announcement came just hours after Rahm told reporters he still had a contract that he was "more than willing to fulfil", with the Spaniard still reportedly having more than $100m remaining on the multi-year contract signed at the end of 2023.

Rahm was one of three players to reject the PGA Tour's Returning Player Program introduced earlier this year, with DeChambeau and Cameron Smith also electing against taking the same pathway back that Brooks Koepka accepted.

All three past major champions are among LIV Golf's largest creditors, with Dustin Johnson understood to be another, while PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp said at the Tour Championship there was no plan to reintroduce the program for next season.

There is still plenty to be determined, but it could leave them all facing a similar journey back to the PGA Tour that Patrick Reed currently faces. The Masters champion is set for a card via finishing inside the top 10 of the DP World Tour's Race to Dubai rankings.

Many of LIV Golf participants were still active DP World Tour members and could elect to play their next season, although it remains unclear whether players would be able to compete on both circuits - like has been seen in recent years - going forward.

What are LIV Golf's plans for next season?

LIV Golf remains hopeful of launching a new iteration of the league in 2027, with events planned in "places like" Australia, South Africa, Mexico, England, Hong Kong and the United States.

Its proposal includes expanding fields to 75 players, with cuts and additional pathways - including Monday qualifiers - added to the events, with more teams embracing national identities.

"I have often said that our role in golf should be to complete, not compete," O'Neil added. "I believe that more strongly today than ever. I know that the next phase of LIV Golf will be an important part of a healthier global golf ecosystem.

"It will create more opportunity for players, bring elite golf to more parts of the world, and give teams and players a real stake in the future they are building.

"Transitions are rarely easy, but they are powerful when you know where you are going. And we do."

articles.title: Rahm busca igualar a Seve en Irlanda, donde Trump podría entregar el trofeo al campeón
articles.standfirst: El español, tras la bancarrota del LIV , y McIlroy aspiran a ganar por tercera vez el Abierto de Irlanda, que se juega en un campo del presidente de Estados Unidos
articles.summary: El español y Rory McIlroy aspiran a ganar por tercera vez el Abierto de Irlanda, que se juega en un campo de Donald Trump, de visita oficial en este país durante el fin de semana
articles.body: Jon Rahm y Rory McIlroy llegan al Abierto de Irlanda con la intención de entrar en el selecto club de multicampeones del torneo, 'cerrado' desde hace 25 años. Fue en 2001 cuando Colin Montgomerie ganó por tercera vez esta cita, un hito que comparte con Seve Ballesteros, Bernhard Langer y Nick Faldo. El español y Rory McIlroy están un peldaño por debajo con dos títulos. El irlandés defiende corona (ganó por primera vez en 2016). Lo hará en el Trump International Golf Links & Hotel Irlanda, en Doonbeg. Se espera la presencia del presidente de Estados Unidos y que se encargue de entregar el trofeo al campeón. Rahm se estrenó en 2017. Fue el tercer golfista español en aparecer en el palmarés tras el mencionado Ballesteros, José María Olazábal y Sergio García. Dos años más tarde, repitió triunfo. El de Barrika llega al evento, nacido en 1927 y en el DP World Tour desde 1975, tras ganar el anillo del LIV Golf por tercera vez y tras anunciarse la bancarrota del circuito saudí. Jon su principal acreedor. Le deben 7,47 millones de dólares y el futuro de su contrato es de lo más incierto. Irlanda es la primera parada en el calendario de Rahm en Europa donde también jugaría el BMW PGA Championship de Wentworth, del 17 al 20 de septiembre, el Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, del 1 al 4 de octubre, y el Open de España, del 8 al 11 de octubre, a expensas de cuando su mujer dé a luz a su cuarto hijo. Rahm vive su décimo aniversario como profesional: "Me hace sentir viejo. He logrado mucho. Estoy muy contento con lo que he hecho hasta ahora. Obviamente, como competidor, siempre hay momentos en los que pienso que debería haber hecho más, ¿verdad? Todos queremos ganar más. Pero he tenido muchísima suerte de jugar a este deporte a un nivel muy alto, y espero poder seguir haciéndolo durante la próxima década", declaró al DP World Tour. Entre los aspirantes al título, Shane Lowry busca reencontrarse con la victoria individual cuatro años después de su último triunfo. El golfista irlandés terminó decimoquinto el pasado año y vuelve a ser una de las principales esperanzas de la afición local. También tendrán protagonismo McKibbin, tras ser sexto en el Masters británico, además de los veteranos Padraig Harrington y Seamus Power. Desde el LIV llegan Tyrrell Hatton, Joaquín Niemann y Tom McKibbin. El torneo contará con Luke Donald, Robert MacIntyre, Sepp Straka, Nicolai y Rasmus Hojgaard, así como con Brooks Koepka, cinco veces ganador de un 'major' y que tratará de desquitarse de su actuación en 2025 cuando no pasó el corte. La representación española la completan Sergio García, Eugenio Chacarra, con dos victorias este curso en el DP World Tour (KLM Open y Open de Italia), Nacho Elvira, Alejandro del Rey, Ángel Hidalgo, Pablo Larrazábal, David Puig, Ángel Ayora, Jorge Campillo, Manuel Elvira, Rafa Cabrera Bello, Iván Cantero, Sebastián García, Quim Vidal y Rocco Repetto Taylor y Adri Arnaus. El Trump International Golf Links & Hotel, diseñado originalmente por Greg Norman y remodelado por Martin Hawtree, se estrena como sede del Abierto de Irlanda. Se espera la asistencia de su propietario, el presidente de los Estados Unidos. Donald Trump llegará a Irlanda este sábado en una visita de dos días en la que se reunirá con la presidenta irlandesa Catherine Connolly y mantendrá una reunión bilateral con el Micheál Martin, primer ministro irlandés. El domingo iría al torneo e incluso podría ser el encargado de entregar el trofeo al campeón.

articles.title: ‘Overdue first step’: UK reacts to gov’t ban on Israeli settlement trade
articles.summary: UK bans imports from illegal Israeli settlements in a strong policy move after recognising a Palestinian state last year.
articles.body:
The United Kingdom has announced it will ban imports originating from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, marking one of London’s strongest policy moves on Israel-Palestine since it formally recognised a Palestinian state last year.

Addressing the UK parliament on Tuesday, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Israel was carrying out “ethnic cleansing” in Palestine and reiterated the British government’s position that Israeli settlements across the occupied West Bank are illegal under international law.

Miliband said allowing settlement-made products to be sold in Britain risked contributing to the occupation, arguing that he did not believe the British public wanted such goods on store shelves.

The measures come as pogroms by Israeli settlers against Palestinian communities in the occupied West Bank intensify and Israel pushes ahead with its contentious expansion of illegal settlements.

Miliband said that Canada and France will also impose a ban on goods from illegal Israeli settlements, while Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Poland, Portugal and Sweden have pledged to “support further action”.

Israel responded by announcing a series of retaliatory measures against the UK. They include barring 12 British MPs from entering Israel and shutting the British consulate in Jerusalem.

Domestically, the reaction was mixed, with many Labour politicians backing the move, while the Conservatives took a more critical stance on Miliband’s announcement.

Here is how UK politicians and others reacted to the government’s decision:

Leader of the opposition Conservatives Kemi Badenoch criticised the move, writing in the UK media outlet The Sun that Miliband’s measures were “performative politics, designed to appease Labour MPs and activists regardless of the consequences for Britain”.

“And those consequences could be serious. Israel is an important security and intelligence partner for the United Kingdom.”

Shadow Foreign Secretary Tom Tugendhat said, “turning Israel into a pariah will risk sectarian division in our own country and risk a further rise in antisemitic violence on our own streets”.

In a statement, the party “welcomed restrictions on trade with illegal Israeli settlements as an overdue first step”, but said the measures must be “strengthened and followed by wider action to end British complicity in Israel’s illegal occupation and the ongoing genocide in Gaza”.

“Greens have long campaigned for a settlement trade ban and are calling for comprehensive restrictions on goods, services and investment in both directions, covering all illegal settlements with no loopholes,” it said.

“The party has called for a full two-way arms embargo, wide-ranging sanctions and an end to military and intelligence cooperation with Israel.”

Party leader Zack Polanski said he was “proud” that Green MPs had been “staunch in standing up for peace” following Israel’s announcement that they would be banned from entering Israel.

“I’m proud that all of our Green MPs have been staunch in their standing up for peace, standing up for peace in the region for both Israelis and Palestinians, and have also supported Jewish communities in the UK,” he said.

“And so to see the Israeli government ban them, I think is not something we’re particularly concerned about. They’re doing the right thing.”

Responding to Miliband’s statement, Liberal Democrat Foreign Affairs spokesperson, Calum Miller MP, said Labour had “finally abandoned Keir Starmer’s pedestrian approach”.

“The settlement trade ban is a long overdue step in the right direction, but Ministers now need to move with urgency,” he said in a statement.

“The current extremist Israeli cabinet is racing to establish facts on the ground to prevent a two-state solution. Liberal Democrats are calling on the Government to introduce emergency legislation to implement this ban without delay. We must make sure there is no UK complicity in the sustainability of illegal settlements.”

Member of Parliament Richard Tice said, “The putrid stench of antisemitism was clear for all to see in the House of Commons.”

“As a result of Miliband’s sanctions, British Jews are less safe and our US security relationship is hugely damaged,” he wrote on X.

Ephraim Mirvis described Miliband’s announcement as a”dark day for British Jews”, and that it would only succeed in “bolstering the very extremism they seek to target”.

Corbyn, a former Labour leader, said sanctions on illegal settlements are welcome, but not enough.

“Britain must end all arms sales, all military cooperation, and all forms of support that sustain Israel’s system of apartheid, occupation and genocide,” he added.

He was among 12 MPs banned from Israel, who said he will “keep speaking up for peace, freedom and justice for the Palestinian people”.

“Strong agreement across the world on today’s UK action against illegal settlements and settler violence that are an existential threat to the two-state solution,” the Health Secretary said on X.

“No one should be profiting from stolen land.”

articles.title: Troubled league LIV Golf files for bankruptcy protection in US
articles.summary: LIV Golf says it intends to restructure its business with a $49.6m bankruptcy loan provided by the Saudi PIF.
articles.body:
Less than five years after it held its first event and created a schism in professional golf, LIV Golf has filed for bankruptcy protection in New Jersey, United States.

The Chapter 11 bankruptcy, or reorganisation bankruptcy, filed on Tuesday, allows the debtor to remain in possession and operate its business, according to US Courts.

The move offers a rare window into the league’s financial state, with LIV Golf owing between $500m and $1bn in estimated liabilities to at least 1,000 creditors, including star players like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm.

The filing listed several other high-profile golfers as creditors still owed millions in unsecured claims. Spaniard Rahm has the largest claim among players at $7.5m, followed by DeChambeau ($5.7m), Dustin Johnson ($5.5m), Cameron Smith of Australia ($4.8m), Tyrrell Hatton of England ($3.4m) and Brooks Koepka ($1.7m). Koepka left the league at the start of 2026.

The bankruptcy filing was widely expected after LIV axed the majority of its staff earlier this month and scrapped its season-ending team championship in August after losing the backing of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF).

Since LIV’s launch in 2022, PIF had poured an estimated $5bn into the tour before abruptly pulling the plug.

The PIF will now provide a loan worth nearly $50m for the bankruptcy and reorganisation process, the LIV statement showed.

LIV’s decision to file for bankruptcy is not a sign that it is dissolving, but rather a step towards restructuring and continuing the PGA Tour competitor under a new business plan.

Tour officials have previously pledged that a “2.0” version of the tour will re-emerge under new investors next season, with a shorter schedule and reduced prize money.

CEO Scott O’Neil published a letter to fans addressing the filing. “Now it is time to enter the next phase of LIV Golf,” he wrote.

“Today, we took an important step forward to get there. LIV Golf has entered a court-supervised restructuring process that provides us with the time and framework to address previous financial obligations and complete a transaction that will make the League’s next phase a reality. Put simply, this process is designed to build a stronger and more sustainable future for LIV Golf.”

O’Neil went on to say LIV intends to continue staging events in some of its more popular international destinations – Australia, South Africa, Mexico, Hong Kong and England among them. The league also will seek to continue playing in the US.

“The next phase of LIV Golf will be built around a sustainable business model and deeper alignment between players and the League, with team golf at its core,” O’Neil wrote.

“Players will have the opportunity to share directly in the value they help create, while teams will be positioned to grow into enduring global sports businesses. And fans will remain at the centre of everything we do.”

But much will depend on whether top stars, including DeChambeau and Rahm, remain.

Widespread reports have linked several LIV stars with potential returns to the PGA Tour and other series, though the PGA said it currently has no plans to offer LIV players a pathway back.

The filing confirmed LIV has partnered for the restructuring effort with British investment group BC Partners.

articles.title: Green Bay Packers’ offensive line uncertainty creates intriguing Week 1 question
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers still have some uncertainty along their offensive line heading into their Week 1 matchup with the Minnesota Vikings. With the 2026 NFL...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers still have some uncertainty along their offensive line heading into their Week 1 matchup with the Minnesota Vikings . With the 2026 NFL season set to begin Wednesday night when the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks revisit their Super Bowl matchup, Green Bay is still waiting on clarity regarding which linemen will take the field for the early divisional showdown.

Packers appear to have their preferred offensive line figured out, but injuries have left two starting spots uncertain heading into Week 1. Left guard Aaron Banks and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele remain questionable for Sunday's matchup with the Vikings, with the team yet to confirm whether either player will be ready to handle a full workload.

The Green Bay Packers' uncertainty at the O-line

"The Green Bay Packers don't know who's starting on their offensive line Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings, or at least they're not revealing that information," wrote The Athletic's Matt Schneidman on his article.

"The two most veteran starters on Green Bay's offensive line are left guard Aaron Banks and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele. … Both finished camp on the field, but coaches this week are making it sound like their statuses aren't certain for the season opener."

Green Bay could be keeping the Vikings guessing by withholding their offensive line plans, but it is unclear how much of an advantage that actually provides. Would Brian Flores adjust his blitz packages based on whether Banks or Bako-Bewele is available, or are the Packers simply trying to keep a division rival from knowing its plans? With the season opener approaching, the answer should become clear soon enough.

"Maybe it's just gamesmanship, but it's fair to wonder whether those uncertainties are legitimate." the NFL insider added.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy predicts players will 'leave LIV Golf' as he questions appeal of revamped league
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy believes the DP World Tour will become much stronger should LIV Golf players choose to return; Sky News understands LIV Golf are hosting negotiations with its players over their futures; watch the Amgen Irish Open live on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
On Tuesday, LIV Golf said it was working with its new lead investor, BC Partners, to restructure and relaunch a new version of the league next year , dubbed LIV 2.0, and as part of that arrangement, it had filed for bankruptcy protection in a New Jersey Court.

The move comes after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced in April it was cutting funding to the rebel league at the end of the 2026 season, after it had burned through $5bn (£3.6bn) over the past five years since its inception in 2021.

Sky News understands that LIV Golf players are currently holding negotiations with the league over whether they will continue to play on the circuit into 2027 or leave.

Stars including Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau have previously been coy on their futures, but the former told reporters on Tuesday that he had a contract with LIV Golf that he was "more than willing to fulfil".

While McIlroy has previously warned it could be a 'tough road back' to the DP World Tour and PGA Tour for LIV Golf players , he added on Wednesday that their addition would only help to make the tours more competitive.

"I'm not in their shoes, but LIV 1.0 at the start looked a lot more attractive than what LIV 2.0 might be from a financial standpoint," McIlroy said ahead of this week's Amgen Irish Open.

"I'm not trying to predict the future, but I would predict that you'll see some guys leave [LIV Golf].

"That means other tours have decisions to make. Obviously there's a lot of players on LIV that can strengthen golf tournaments and make them more competitive. So I would see that as a good thing for the DP World Tour."

Rahm and his Legion XIII team-mate Tyrrell Hatton are both set to tee up at the Amgen Irish Open, and will also play at next week's BMW PGA Championship.

And McIlroy believes the inclusion of LIV players going forward will only make the DP World Tour stronger.

"The health of the DP World Tour is in a really good spot," McIlroy added. "They have a wonderful alliance with the PGA Tour. I think that alliance is only going to get stronger, especially with the PGA Tour committing to working with the DP World Tour for some of these international events at this time of the year going forward.

"So you have PGA Tour players really with nothing to do for five months in this period. If whoever else is incorporated into these tournaments, that makes them more competitive.

"Overall, with the way things are working out, it's a very good thing for the golf ecosystem. It only makes these tournaments stronger with more competitive players in them."

Donald: LIV players will be thinking about the Ryder Cup

Ahead of the 2027 Ryder Cup at Adare Manor, European captain Luke Donald admitted some ambiguity still lingers over who might choose to continue playing on LIV Golf.

However, he added the chance to play in the Ryder Cup could sway their decision.

"There's still some uncertainty," Donald said. "Time will tell to see where those guys land. Obviously, you want your best players available, and you want them playing as many counting events as possible.

"You set your qualification system to try and determine who those top six guys are, and the more someone like a Jon Rahm or Tyrrell Hatton, if they are playing more events on the DP World Tour, they are going to have a better opportunity to fill one of those top six. So that's obviously great.

"If not, we'll see what happens. But I don't really determine their schedules or where they play. But I know a lot of these guys, the Ryder Cup is high up on their priority list. So I'm sure they will be thinking about that."

articles.title: LIV bankruptcy protection: What next for the players on PGA and DP World Tour?
articles.summary: Golf's main tours are expecting a lot of interest in rejoining from LIV golfers – but the path back might not be so easy.
articles.body:
The DP World Tour has said it has had a "high volume" of interest from LIV Golf players and is exploring ways to accommodate those who leave the breakaway league.

It comes as LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy protection in the US on Tuesday , as it attempts to restructure for a "new era" next year.

LIV owes at least $45m (£33m) to 14 current and former players.

Its golfers, including star names like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm, can now opt to leave, rather than being obliged to see out their contracts in LIV 2.0 which is aiming to launch next year.

But, given all the acrimony since LIV's launch in 2021 and subsequent outlay of $5bn (£3.7bn) split the sport, it may not be easy to return to the PGA Tour and DP World Tour.

A spokesperson for the DP World Tour said: "Given the high volume of inbound interest and enquiries we have received in recent weeks, we are exploring the terms on which we are willing to accommodate players, provided they are free from third-party contractual restrictions and are willing to abide by our membership regulations.

"Our tournament committee has approved the process we intend to follow and we expect further enquiries in the days ahead."

Court documents show LIV estimates its assets at $100m-$500m (£74m-£370m) and its liabilities at between $500m and $1bn (£370m-£739m).

Plans are for LIV 2.0 to be "built around a sustainable business model".

It is unclear at present how many of LIV's existing players may decide to stay.

LIV files for bankruptcy protection with over $45m owed to players

'Time will tell' - Rahm on LIV Golf future

Strained smiles and uncertainty - the strange end of LIV Golf 1.0

Playing on both the traditional tours and LIV has proved complicated.

There are now believed to be around 15 players who have exemptions to compete in in the DP World Tour.

Nine players, including Rahm, agreed conditional releases this year which allowed them to feature on both tours without disciplinary action.

The PGA said this was one of the "largest financial repercussions in professional sports history" under its returning member programme for top players.

Conversely, Patrick Reed did not meet the programme's criteria when he quit LIV.

He has therefore had to earn his place back on next year's PGA Tour through the DP World Tour's Race to Dubai top 10.

PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said last month there were "no current plans" to run the returning member programme again, which indicated Reed's path back will be the most likely way forward for other golfers.

BBC Sport has been told players who have exempt status will be able to apply to the DP World Tour, but the tour would need to consider what any new LIV looks like before a final decision.

For those without exempt status rejoining the DP World Tour, it is understood they could not be contracted to LIV.

If LIV can secure the funding to continue with what they are calling LIV 2.0, the major scaling back will be in terms of prize funds.

Their ambition is for tournaments worth around £7m, which puts them well below leading events on the PGA Tour but above most competitions on Europe's DP World Tour.

LIV bosses are looking to expand events from 57 to 75 players, have Monday qualifying events and introduce halfway cuts while retaining a team aspect.

Whether this arrangement is enough to attract the bigger names is open to question.

Significantly, Rahm said this week he was prepared to fulfil his contract with LIV 1.0, with no mention of any commitment to the intended new iteration.

The two-time major winner is expected to be among a number of players who will depart with the intention of finding a way back on to the PGA Tour.

One of LIV's biggest challenges will be to find a playing roster of sufficient quality to attract the required investment to make LIV 2.0 viable.

Is there a clear path back to main tours for LIV players?

The short answer is no and a number of LIV players are potentially facing career limbo.

LIV golfers are automatically banned for a year by the PGA Tour. It took the returning player programme, a special arrangement offered to a select few, to make it possible for Koepka to go back to the US circuit earlier this year.

Rahm, DeChambeau and Cameron Smith rejected that deal to stay on at LIV.

The PGA Tour has shown no enthusiasm for reinstating that arrangement but will, no doubt, be monitoring developments over coming weeks.

The DP World Tour offers a pathway because the leading 10 players on the European circuit currently gain access to PGA Tour membership.

This is the route being taken by Reed, who left LIV ahead of its 2026 season. So in the short term, it could be a boon for the European-based circuit to have the likes of Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton competing regularly next year.

Potential complications lie in the details of how the PGA Tour will structure its two-tier format from 2028. How many leading DP World Tour players from the 2027 season will be eligible for the upper-tier Championship series of tournaments?

The European tour also has to decide how to treat LIV players next season. In 2026, it struck a deal which allowed certain players, including Rahm and Hatton, to play LIV events without sanction.

That deal is thought unlikely to be offered next year.

Have traditional tours won battle for golf?

Yes, because they have withstood the loss of huge names to a breakaway tour that has been financed to the tune of $5bn and that tour has now filed for bankruptcy protection.

For five years, the PGA Tour has been functioning without some of the biggest stars in the game. And to ensure not losing more talent, it has needed to bolster prize funds and restructure its future path by creating a for-profit business model.

It is entitled to be bullish though, especially with $1.5bn investment from the Strategic Sports Group.

But no-one knows how sustainable it will be to stage a full season of $20m tournaments. Since LIV arrived, the price of staging top-level tournaments has grown massively, with most of that money flowing into players' pockets.

At the moment, the DP World Tour looks to have emerged stronger by offering a path back to the golf establishment for those golfers who do not want to hang around for LIV 2.0.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Nelly Korda plays down 'intimidation factor' to Team Europe as Charley Hull eyes rematch with world No 1
articles.summary: Nelly Korda headlines Team USA at the Solheim Cup, who look to retain the trophy in the Netherlands; Charley Hull makes her eighth consecutive appearance for Team Europe; watch Solheim Cup live on Friday from 6am on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Hull makes an eighth consecutive Solheim Cup appearance for Team Europe, who look to regain the trophy at Bernardus Golf - live on Sky Sports - after losing on American soil two years ago.

The 30-year-old top-scored for Team Europe in their 2024 defeat and despatched Korda 6&4 during the Sunday singles, with Hull open to facing the world No 1 again for Anna Nordqvist's side during their pursuit of a home victory.

"Playing Nelly Korda at that time was really good - it was so much fun," Hull said in her pre-tournament press conference. "I came out and played pretty well.

"Every dog has its day and I also did that day, but she's had a pretty incredible season so far this year. If it came down to singles, it would be a really good match.

"I have a lot of respect for Nelly [Korda]. She's a great world No 1, a great golfer and anything can happen in match play."

Hull and Carlota Ciganda are the players heading into the week with most Solheim Cup experience, having both played in every edition since 2013, although the Englishwoman doesn't put any extra pressure on herself as a 'veteran' of Team Europe.

"I see my role as a player, really," Hull insisted. "I do my own thing, trying to keep my own routine as much as you can. The captains are there for advice - the younger players [can] come and ask me some advice and stuff.

"We've got here from playing our normal routine. Every week we're by our ourselves, so we really shouldn't do anything too differently. We've still got to hit a ball around the golf course and play good!"

Korda makes her fifth consecutive Solheim Cup appearance and arrives in the Netherlands as the dominant force in the women's game, having won four times on the LPGA Tour - including the first two majors of the year - in an impressive season.

The 28-year-old has one of the best winning percentages of any American in Solheim Cup history, forming an unbeaten foursomes partnership with Allisen Corpuz in the last two editions, with Andrea Lee hoping that Korda can Team USA an edge.

"We all respect her a lot and we look up to her," Lee said. "She has an amazing game and she's the No 1 player in the world, so it's just really nice to have her on our side.

"I feel like it almost brings a little bit of an intimidation factor going against Europe, so we have a little bit of an up just because we have her."

"Honestly, I don't even think about that," Korda insisted. "I remain in my bubble and I'm a little bit oblivious to it all, but because I want to be. I just want to make it really simple for myself, not to think about too much and just to go out and play my game.

"What I love about this tournament is how much passion it brings from each side. Even when Europe becomes very passionate about what they're doing on the golf course, I feel like we all want to elevate our game as well.

"As for a target, I don't really think about it. If they're intimidated, great! But for me, I just go out and do my thing. I just hope that the United States team just brings a lot of passion."

articles.title: Ryder Cup: Securing spot for Adare Manor a 'big part' of Shane Lowry's motivation
articles.summary: Shane Lowry says it is time to get himself "in gear" if he is to secure his spot on Europe's Ryder Cup team for Adare Manor next year.
articles.body:
Shane Lowry says it is time to get himself "in gear" if he is to secure his spot on Europe's Ryder Cup team for Adare Manor next year.

The 2019 Open champion is in the field at the Irish Open this week, with the qualification process for the 2027 Ryder Cup, to be held in County Limerick from 17-19 September, having commenced last month.

Irishman Lowry was a member of the European teams in 2021, 2023 and 2025, holing the winning putt in the latter event at Bethpage Black.

The 39-year-old has, however, fallen from 26th to 53rd in the world rankings over the course of 2026 in a season characterised by frustrating near-misses.

While Lowry said performing well in front of an Irish crowd at Doonbeg this week would always be a "carrot dangling", there is an added significance knowing each tournament between now and next August could bring him closer to the long-held goal of playing in a Ryder Cup on home soil.

"When that was announced, you look at the dates, look at how old you'll be, and that's been a big big goal of mine," Lowry told BBC Sport NI's Stephen Watson.

"To be part of a home Ryder Cup team is amazing, but to be part of one in Ireland would be very, very cool.

"It goes without saying, Ryder Cup points have started so it's time to get myself in gear and get on that team. That's going to be a big part of my motivation over the next 12 months."

Irish Open will feel 'different' with Trump visit

'Time will tell' - Rahm on LIV Golf future

Lowry is one of seven players from the victorious 2025 team who will be teeing it up at the Irish Open this week.

With Adare Manor just 60 miles from Doonbeg, Europe captain Luke Donald has arranged a meeting of 16 prospective team members at the first Irish course to stage the biennial event since the K Club in 2006.

Among the group will be potential Ryder Cup rookies Alex Fitzpatrick, Eugenio Chacarra, Kristoffer Reitan and Angel Ayora, although Donald is also keen to get more experienced players acquainted with a venue best known for staging the JP McManus Pro-Am.

"I did some off how strong some of the guys are playing statistically and a few of my own picks," said Donald of how he decided on the group that will gather on Sunday and Monday.

"I think it's just an opportunity to see the course. Eight or nine of the guys have never played it. The more we can get out and familiarise ourselves, it'll stand us in good stead."

Donald feels the demise of LIV Golf could potentially make his selection process more straightforward this time around.

The Englishman, who first became captain for the 2023 event after planned skipper Henrik Stenson switched to the breakaway tour, had LIV players Tyrrell Hatton and Jon Rahm in his team last year, although he had to use a wildcard pick on the latter.

After LIV filed for bankruptcy protection in the US on Tuesday, players are now free to leave rather than see out their contracts and the DP World Tour has already said there has been a "high volume" of interest.

That could mean prospective team members playing in a greater number of events where Ryder Cup points are on offer.

"I think you always want the six guys who qualify automatically to be the strongest," Donald added.

"If that's Jon and Tyrrell playing more and playing more here where the points are, that gives them more opportunities to qualify. That's a good thing."

articles.title: Fifth day of rail disruption west of Paddington
articles.summary: Disruption continues to rail services in London after a fire to cables on the weekend.
articles.body:
Rail passengers face a fifth day of reduced services west of London Paddington after a fire damaged power equipment beside the tracks.

The Elizabeth line is running only two trains an hour to Heathrow and Reading, while Great Western Railway and Heathrow Express services have also been cut.

The fire broke out at Scrubs Lane in Kensal Green on Saturday afternoon, damaging an electrical substation and cabling supplying the overhead lines.

British Transport Police said a man was arrested on suspicion of arson and has been released on bail.

All lines between Paddington and Heathrow and Reading were blocked on Saturday, and almost 400 passengers had to be escorted from a train that lost power after overhead cables caught fire.

London Fire Brigade said six fire engines and about 40 firefighters attended.

National Rail said the full electric timetable could not run between Paddington and Reading until repairs were finished, because of the demands it would place on the electrical distribution system.

Elizabeth line trains are running twice an hour to Heathrow Terminal 4, Heathrow Terminal 5, Maidenhead and Reading, with some calling additionally at Acton Main Line, Hanwell, Iver, Langley and Taplow.

GWR services are calling at Slough, Maidenhead and Twyford on a reduced timetable, and the Heathrow Express is running less frequently. Intercity services are largely unaffected because they can run on diesel through the damaged section.

A statement on GWR's website said the fire had been "due to vandalism of railway equipment".

Transport for London advised passengers to allow more time and to check before travelling. It said train times and frequencies might differ from the usual timetable.

The disruption is expected to last until at least the end of Wednesday.

articles.title: Luke Donald builds trust with future European Ryder Cup team
articles.summary: Luke Donald is gathering 16 potential European Ryder Cup players at Adare Manor to build relationships, trust and familiarity with the course.
articles.body:
Luke Donald isn't wasting time getting potential members of the 2027 European Ryder Cup team together at Adare Manor.

As first reported by The Scotsman's Martin Dempster, Donald, who returns as Team Europe's captain for a third tour of duty, has arranged for 16 players to gather at the 2027 Ryder Cup venue following this week's Amgen Irish Open at Trump International Golf Links at Doonbeg, which is around 60 miles from Adare Manor.

"It's always good to see the guys and just check in. I haven't played a lot this year. So much more ideal having those sort of face-to-face conversations, some have dinners, just catch up," Donald said on Wednesday during a press conference ahead of the DP World Tour event. "I think that communication, that chat, just is beneficial in the long run. It creates some good relationships and good trust."

Donald noted that he was "keeping an eye on a bunch of players," and confirmed that four potential rookies have been invited to the team building exercise: Alex Fitzpatrick and Kristoffer Reitan, who both won on the PGA Tour season this season and are the top candidates for PGA Tour Rookie of the Year, and a pair of Spaniards in Eugenio Chacarra, a two-time winner on the DP World Tour, and promising 21-year-old bomber Angel Ayora, who recorded 10 top-10 finishes as a DP World Tour rookie.

The players participating in the gathering will make their way to Wentworth in England afterwards to prep for the BMW PGA Championship next week.

But first Donald is going to get a closer look this week at the younger Fitzpatrick as well as 23-year-old Northern Irishman Tom McKibbin. It's no accident he is paired with them in the first two rounds of the Irish Open.

"One of the privileges is I do tend to, most weeks when I'm playing over here, get to choose my pairings. I think Alex Fitzpatrick, obviously speaks for itself how well he's done off the back of his win with his brother at Zurich. He's really kicked on amazingly well, showing that his game holds up against some of the very best on the U.S. tour. Tremendous strong finish at the Tour Championship," Donald said. "Tom is someone I've played a couple times with before. Certainly I think he played quite well a couple weeks ago at the British Masters. Statistically, I think he's starting to show some improvement. So I'm looking forward to seeing his game as well."

Asked about LIV's bankruptcy and how it could effect qualifying for the Euro side, Donald said, "there's still some uncertainty. I think time will tell to see where those guys land. Obviously very consistent through my captaincy that you want your best players available, and you want them playing as many counting events as possible.

"I think you set your qualification system to try and determine who those top six guys are, and the more someone like a Jon or Tyrrell, if they are playing more events on the DP World Tour, they are going to have a better opportunity to fill one of those top six. So that's obviously great."

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Angel Yin opens up on illness battle, Team USA doubts and how Angela Stanford helped her decision
articles.summary: Angel Yin makes her fourth Solheim Cup appearance, despite a stomach issue leaving her missing the final months of Team USA's qualification campaign for Angela Stanford's side; watch Solheim Cup live on Friday from 6am on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Yin was among the automatic qualifiers via the US Solheim Cup points list for Angela Stanford's side, who are looking to retain the trophy at Bernardus Golf and claim a first away victory over Team Europe since 2015.

The 27-year-old has not completed a 72-hole tournament since May and only played in one LPGA Tour event since June, missing the cut by 13 shots on her return to action from an undisclosed stomach issue.

Yin has lost over two and a half stone in weight from the illness and had seen her participation thrown into doubt, although was left grateful of the support captain Stanford offered when debating her Solheim Cup status.

When asked whether she thought about not playing, Yin said in her pre-tournament press conference: "Yes, of course. I know it's crazy that I'm here because I played a week before in Boston and it obviously wasn't great.

"It wasn't ideal. It [rounds of 81 and 76] is not a score you really bring out and you go 'wow, that's the person that's going to be helping America bring home the Cup'.

"I've been working hard, I've been trying everything I can, because this is the biggest event in women's golf. We know this is going to be a big deal, because this is the 20th Solheim Cup.

"I wanted to be honest, because I would never jeopardise America. I had honest talks with myself in the mirror, with my team, and obviously with Angela [Stanford]. She's the only other person - other than my family - that I've updated throughout all of this.

"We all agreed on this and she wanted me here. I had my caddie ask her: 'Do you want me here?' And if she had said no, I wouldn't be here. But she said yes. With belief like that and confidence from her to back me, why wouldn't I show up?"

Stanford insisted in her press conference on Tuesday that Yin will feature for Team USA , despite former world No 1 Lilia Vu - who claimed a key half-point in the 2024 win - being on-site in uniform and a potential last-minute alternate.

Yin had extra practice on Wednesday, taking the front nine on her own before joining the rest of Team USA on the back nine, with the two-time LPGA Tour winner confident her game is showing positive signs heading into a key week.

"I'm feeling great," Yin added. "I guess everybody has different opinions, but I personally think it [her game] is not bad. Every day it's getting better. I guess it's like art, right? Everybody has a different opinion, but results are the only thing that matters.

"I can say and be confident as much as I want, but ultimately it's up to the captain, because she needs to be responsible for us. I just need to do my part and then I just need to wait for her call.

"Whatever she does and whatever she says will, in my opinion, be the best decision because we trust her and she's been leading us great."

Yin and Yealimi Noh won a practice match again Alison Lee and Megan Khang, who was left impressed by how her team-mate is playing despite her limited competitive golf.

"Angel is playing great golf," Lee insisted. "She's working hard, she's putting in the work, and she's working probably the hardest out here.

"She's working hard, she's putting in the work, and she's working probably the hardest out here. She wants to make the reps, wants to put in the effort.

"She's obviously earned her spot here and she's doing her best to obviously give her best, so there's nothing but great things to say about her."

articles.title: 'An injustice' or 'righting a wrong': British Jews debate sanctions move
articles.summary: The UK's decision to sanction trade with illegal settlements has prompted a range of opinion among the British Jewish community.
articles.body:
From his home in the occupied West Bank settlement of Efrat, British-Israeli Rabbi Leo Dee wrote an open letter to Andy Burnham on Wednesday, accusing him of deciding "to single out Jewish Israelis like me for economic punishment".

The rabbi's British-born wife Lucy, and their daughters Maia and Rina, were killed by Palestinians in the occupied West Bank in 2023. They were shot dead as they drove through the Jordan Valley.

"I am enraged at the injustice of the situation," he told the BBC, claiming the government's decision to place sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements, and not the Palestinian authority, was hypocritical.

He said Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband was "living in a different universe", and argued that the main group who would face hardship as a result were the hundreds of Palestinians who were employed in them.

Settlements are illegal under international law, and there has been a rise in violence towards Palestinians in the occupied West Bank by settlers since the start of the Gaza war, which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.

Miliband said the sanctions, announced after Israel opened up tenders for the construction of some 1,200 settlement homes, were necessary to safeguard the possibility of a two-state solution - and to ensure the UK "not only calls out injustice and suffering, but acts".

Where is Israel's proposed West Bank settlement the UK opposes?

How Israel is expanding settlements in drive to reshape West Bank

Chris Mason: Burnham looks to show he will go further than Starmer with West Bank sanctions

Rabbi Dee said he believed that, apart from a small group of "hooligan settlers" who could not be controlled and whom most people do not support, many others wanted a different outcome.

"Ninety-nine percent actually want to work closer with Palestinians" and have peaceful relations with them, he said, just as he did "before the 7 October attacks".

Another British rabbi was also in the West Bank as the UK government made its announcement - and takes a different view.

Rabbi Jonathan Wittenberg was in the Palestinian village of Umm al-Khair, visiting the family of Awdeh Hathaleen, a prominent Palestinian activist and English teacher who was shot and killed by an Israeli settler last year .

The Emeritus Rabbi of the New North London synagogue told the BBC he wanted to show that what was happening to Palestinians there mattered to him and his community.

Rabbi Wittenberg said he had "seen with my own eyes several times in the West Bank, the intimidation and threats towards Palestinians - and this needs to be called out".

"It's terrible for Israel and for Israel's future, it's not what Judaism teaches and it's deeply wrong", he added.

Supported by other Rabbis in the liberal and progressive UK Jewish communities, Rabbi Wittenberg believes that it is possible to support Israel, be concerned for the safety of British Jews, and that it is right for the UK government to take action to protect Israelis and Palestinians.

However, he also said he was "extremely sad that it's come to this" and that he shared the "concerns of the Jewish community leadership that people will use this for antisemitism and for demonising Israel even further".

Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis, who represents the Orthodox community, previously said the sanctions marked a "truly dark day" and placed British Jews at greater risk of attacks.

In Golders Green - where ambulances run by a Jewish medical charity were set on fire and two visibly Jewish men were stabbed in what police called a terror attack earlier this year - there was concern the government's actions against Israel would increase attacks against British Jews.

"It's so tricky because, in principle, I agree with opposing these new settlements," Michael Cohen, who works for a Jewish charity, told the BBC.

But he added: "The timing of it, I think, was completely... just self interest for the Labour Party, signalling before a by-election, before the party conference."

He said the practical impact of the move would be "almost zero".

One woman, who runs a jewellery shop that was was twice cordoned off due to incidents in Golders Green, was very critical of the sanctions and said she would "make it my mission" to continue to buy Israeli goods whenever she could.

"We have to [support] our own because no one else is going to", Deborah Miller told the BBC.

At the end of the week, Jewish congregations will celebrate Rosh Hashana, the Jewish New Year.

Police are already increasing security around Jewish areas to protect communities who have faced multiple attacks this year and are fearful of more.

The number of antisemitic incidents recorded across the UK since the start of the year is up by a fifth compared to last year, figures show .

The Community Security Trust (CST), an organisation that provides security support to the Jewish community, recorded 1,926 incidents of anti-Jewish hate across the UK in the first six months of 2026.

The Crime Survey for England and Wales , estimates that only 44% of hate crime incidents between April 2022 and March 2025 came to the attention of the police.

articles.title: GB&I win offered a tonic for European golf fans. But Americans have reason for hope
articles.summary: GB&I celebrates a thrilling Walker Cup win as the team looks toward future venues and new leadership strategies.
articles.body:
Good news, folks. The Walker Cup in 2052 already has a venue.

It's going to be played at Seminole in Florida, so you can scribble that one down in your diary amid all those other things you've already got arranged for that weekend in 26 years' time.

Golf does love a bit of forward planning, doesn't it? In the wake of GB&I's thrilling, last-gasp Walker Cup triumph at Lahinch, a thing came through in the post-event paraphernalia reminding me of the future dates and host courses for the transatlantic duel.

I gazed at it and gave the kind of shuddering grimace you'd get from a toddler when you give them a teaspoon of cod liver oil.

In 2052, God willing, I'll be 76. Presumably, I'll have been put out to pasture, or at least put out of my misery, by then.

On the other hand, though, golf writing can be a business of tremendous longevity, and each passing year for a scribe brings added appreciation and gravitas.

"You're not going anywhere," said the sports editor. This, of course, was less a comment on his determination to retain my services, more a reflection on a writing career that's as stagnant as a blocked culvert.

Oh well, roll on 2052, eh? The Walker Cup of 2026, meanwhile, will live long in the memory.

Last week, I mulled over GB&I's 1971 Walker Cup win and documented how the triumph made front-page news in Scotland.

It was wonderful sporting theatre, without the overblown jingoism and commercial claptrap of, say, a Ryder Cup . The Walker Cup remains one for the purists.

Sunday's showdown was a terrific advert for amateur golf and the spirit of its competition. GB&I's edge-of-the-seat conquest was a timely tonic too after five US wins in a row.

There have often been murmurings that the Walker Cup should expand to incorporate a wider European team, like the Ryder Cup did in 1979 after a series of ritual thrashings for GB&I.

That, of course, didn't go down well with a'body. "So, the Ryder Cup is dead," wrote the esteemed golf writer, Peter Dobereiner, at the time.

"It was quietly put down to prevent further suffering, and the body was interred in an unmarked grave."

Check out the best photos from the 2026 Walker Cup at Lahinch

I assume many stout traditionalists would feel the same about such a change to the Walker Cup. Sunday's win, though, showed that there's plenty of life in GB&I yet.

We know that Uncle Sam's lads have always dominated this affair – they have 40 wins to GB&I's 10 since the event's inception back in 1922 – but a first defeat for the USA since 2015 gives this treasured tussle fresh vigor. A turn up for the books is always nice, isn't it?

Well, unless you're an American. The USGA, custodians of the amateur game on this side of the pond, have made a concerted effort in recent years to accelerate the conveyor belt of domestic talent. Given the sheer numbers in this land of plenty, it's a huge belt.

The National Development Program, launched in 2023, is the country's first unified initiative designed to create a clear pathway from junior golf right through to the elite end.

"They will get it right too," said David Inglis, the Scottish exile who is a leading coach at Chicago's Northwestern University, in a conversation with this correspondent recently.

"Over the next five to 10 years, they will churn out a lot of good players."

GB&I have been warned. For the time being, though, they can savor this very sweet success.

Nobody will be prouder than Dean Robertson, the canny Scot who has relished his two stints as GB&I skipper and has approached the task with the kind of attention to detail you'd get with a CT scan.

His first outing as captain may have ended in a heavy defeat at Cypress Point, but his second term brought a shimmering silver lining after an historic comeback.

I imagine a bronze bust of Dean will be getting plonked on the Bow Butts in St Andrews. And they could chisel out another one for the clubhouse at Cochrane Castle.

Robertson broke the mould as GB&I's first professional captain. It was always going to happen.

For years, there were concerns that the R&A were simply running out of skippers in an age when the career amateur is almost as old-fashioned as the thatched roof.

Opening up the post to former Walker Cup players, who subsequently turned professional, provides a healthy list of potential candidates going forward. Rory McIlroy as captain in 2052?

Robertson, a Walker Cupper himself back in 1993, revelled in the role. And you never know. Like Luke Donald with the European Ryder Cup team, Robertson might get a third crack at the Walker Cup in 2028? If it ain't broke and all that.

The team golf comes thick and fast with the leading women of Europe and the USA taking centre stage in this weekend's Solheim Cup .

After GB&I's showstopping amateur dramatics on Sunday, the professionals have a hard act to follow.

articles.title: Packers tackle Zach Bako-Bewele says he plans to start against Vikings
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele says he's a go for Week 1, and his surgically repaired right knee isn't an issue.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY – Green Bay Packers right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele said more was made about whether he would be ready to play against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Sept. 13, than was probably necessary.

He said he plans to be in the starting lineup.

More than a week ago, Bako-Bewele said he wanted to make sure he was able to make it through an entire game before committing to starting against the Vikings .

On Sept. 9, he said he meant endurance more than the condition of his right knee, which he had repaired in January. Bako-Bewele had been practicing regularly, but in spurts, making sure he wasn't trying to do too much too fast.

When he spoke after camp had ended, the most work he had had was in the joint practice with the Arizona Cardinals . He said he got through that with some soreness afterward and wanted to see how practice went over the next week and a half.

"I think the plan was always to be ready Week 1," he said. "I had given an answer a couple of weeks ago where it sounded like I was unsure. But I think it got blown out of proportion. I was referring more to getting in shape, getting back with team, and the rhythm of playing."

Bako-Bewele was a limited participant in the Sept. 9 padded practice, but limited can mean he just sat out for a few snaps instead of taking every snap.

Whatever the case, it appears the Packers will have at least four-fifths of the offensive line available for the opener at U.S. Bank Stadium.

The only question mark is left guard Aaron Banks , who also was a limited participant. Banks wasn't available for comment on whether he planned to play.

articles.title: HUSKERS HAPPY HOUR: 49-21 Is a Good Start With Plenty To Work On
articles.summary: Huskers football, Ohio, Bowling Green, College Football & even a power outage at the end inhonor of Florida St.
articles.body:
Season 3 of the Huskers Happy Hour kicked off and we had a blazing hot opener vs. the Ohio Bobcats to talk about, so we did. We went through the drive chart, the stats – team and individual – and looked ahead to the next opponent, Bowling Green, who dropped their opener to FCS squad Tarlton State.

The Huskers? They got an early challenge, held their ground, turned things around and finally stopped making the mistakes which made the scoreboard take longer to catch up to Nebraska's control of the game.

We talked about the Nebraska debuts of Anthony Colandrea and true freshman running back Jamal Rule, both of whom looked very good their first time sporting the Husker scarlet.

My wreck, Mylie's wedding, folks being wheeled out of Memorial Stadium and Owen Chambliss unexpectedly not dressing all came up. I also had some opinions on why LSU's absolute destruction of Dabo Sweeney and Clemson gave me so much joy, despite Lane Kiffin being the current CFB public enemy #1.

By the way, apologies to all who were still on with me at the end when our podcasting site went down temporarily.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts credits preparation for his perfect Week 1 record
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts credits preparation, confidence and the team playing together for his perfect record as the Eagles’ starter in season openers
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts has never lost a season opener as the Philadelphia Eagles' starting quarterback, and he believes the record reflects Philadelphia's work long before kickoff. Since replacing Carson Wentz , Hurts is 5-0 in Week 1 starts entering Sunday's opener against the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field. Philadelphia has defeated Atlanta , Detroit , New England , Green Bay and Dallas in its past five openers.

"Keeping the main thing the main thing. Having the time to prepare. And playing together," Hurts said, via Zach Berman . "It's a reflection of the work and the preparation that we've had."

Hurts also pointed to the confidence and clarity that preparation created. Those qualities will be particularly important Sunday as Philadelphia unveils Sean Mannion's offense against a division opponent familiar with the Eagles ' personnel. The circumstances surrounding each opener have changed, but Hurts has consistently helped Philadelphia navigate Week 1 uncertainty. He passed for three touchdowns in a 32-6 victory over Atlanta in 2021 and accounted for 333 total yards in a win over Detroit the following year. Philadelphia's past three opening victories were decided by one score, including last season's 24-20 win over Dallas. Hurts ran for two touchdowns as the Eagles overcame an early deficit.

That history does not guarantee success against Washington. The Eagles have changed offensive coordinators, reworked portions of their receiving corps, and installed new concepts throughout the offseason. Hurts' approach, however, remains unchanged. Preparation creates clarity, and clarity allows the Eagles to play confidently together when Week 1 arrives.

articles.title: Green Bay Packers: Matt LaFleur claps back at question on how Jordan Love can improve in 2026
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers have quite a few questions staring them in face as they prepare for Week One of the 2026 NFL season. And while these questions are subs...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers have quite a few questions staring them in face as they prepare for Week One of the 2026 NFL season. And while these questions are substantial, they have the benefit of having a great starting quarterback in Jordan Love .

Entering his fourth season as Green Bay 's starter under center, Love has command of the team's offense and has the luxury of all of his pass-catching weapons being healthy (something he did not have last season).

Despite not having a healthy slew of receivers in 2025, Love had the best season of his career a year ago. One cannot help but be excited for what he will do in 2026 with all the hype surrounding the offense.

Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur believes Jordan Love is an elite quarterback

On Wednesday, LaFleur was asked by Packers media members what Love has to do to improve this year. He ruffled at the question, stating that he does not understand why people keep asking him that.

"I think he's an elite player," LaFleur said . "I'll let you guys figure that out what the next step is. A lot of times, it's due to team success, and the more success we have, the more people will view him in that light."

Last season, Love had a 66.3% completion percentage, 3,381 passing yards, 23 touchdowns, just six interceptions, and a 101.2 passer rating (15 games). Missing a game due to a concussion and another out of precaution due to the looming postseason caused his numbers to be less than what many might have wanted to see.

LaFleur brings up a good point, though. Obviously, Love continues to practice, improve, and stay sharp every day. However, he has very little left to prove in terms of how good of a quarterback he is. Green Bay's losses last season were not due to poor play by their starting quarterback. Rather, he led them to victory in several games that they otherwise might have lost.

As the Packers head coach states, it may take the team being more successful in order for Love to get the recognition he deserves. Winning the NFC North and making a deep run in the NFL Playoffs would go a long way in silencing the ever-declining number of Love's doubters.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: How  Team USA look to overcome 'heart-breaking' near-misses against Team Europe and retain trophy
articles.summary: Each of the last four Solheim Cups on European soil have produced a winning margin of two points or less; Team Europe look to regain the trophy after their loss to Team USA in 2024; watch Solheim Cup live on Friday from 6am on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Angela Stanford's side arrive at Bernardus Golf as defending champions, following their 15.5-12.5 win over Team Europe in Virginia two years ago, leaving Team USA chasing back-to-back wins for the first time since 2017.

It's 11 years since the United States last won in Europe, when a record final-day comeback overturned a 10-6 deficit and snatched a one-point win in Germany, with Team USA falling agonisingly short in both the last two away editions.

Team USA lost by a point at Gleneagles in 2019 after Suzann Pettersen's iconic putt in the singles, then followed a home loss in 2021 by letting their commanding opening-day lead slip to tie 14-14 at Finca Cortesin in Spain two years later.

"It's always really hard to win on foreign soil," American Andrea Lee said in her press conference. "I think we played really well and came so close last time in Spain.

"It was pretty heart-breaking to end in a tie and for Europe to retain, but I think a lot of us from that team are here this week. We're just very motivated to keep the [Solheim] Cup and try to win on foreign soil again."

Team USA travelled together - including caddies - from Atlanta to the Netherlands on Saturday, spending the following day as tourists in Amsterdam ahead of switching focus to Solheim Cup week.

Attention to detail with the American camp has seen clothing and bag designs linked to past successes on away soil, including their 2007 victory in Sweden before their 2015 win in Germany.

"I think something about this format just brings a fire out of the European girls that they will come out and play amazing golf, and they're great competitors to play against, so I think that's something we're preparing for," Alison Lee explained.

"Obviously coming over here to Europe is always difficult. I don't ever play in the rain or wind, but I think that's something we're all expecting.

"We know that if we come out and do our best to play some good golf, and hopefully have a bit of chemistry out there as well, I think we have a really good chance this year."

Andrea Lee added: " If we win this week, this would be the fourth foreign soil win for the United States. I think we're all just really determined to try and keep it."

The last four Solheim Cups have had a combined winning margin of six points, compared to the 24-point difference in the last four Ryder Cup, with Team USA failing to close out recent opportunities at away success.

"In Spain [2023], we were super close," world No 1 Nelly Korda insisted. "They tied with Europe, so they retained the [Solheim] Cup. For Gleneagles, I feel like we played really well, but maybe haven't had momentum go (our way) while we're in Europe.

"I think that what Ang [Stanford] and the assistants have said this week is to really rely on each other. When it gets tough, we all have to realise we are here for each other and we also have so many people out there supporting us."

On recent disappointments, Angel Yin admitted: "As much as we don't close out the win, it's always coming down to the last putt. We always put up a really good fight, even though we're unfamiliar with the situation, and I think we're learning."

Can Europe claim Solheim Cup on home soil?

Europe's off-course antics in the team room have included ping pong, darts and a quiz involving baby photos of the caddies in recent days, with personalised pictures among the gifts received.

Nordqvist's young line-up contains four rookies and half a squad that's never experienced a home Solheim Cup, with Charley Hull - making an eighth consecutive appearance - among the stars hoping to deliver.

"I actually feel like there's a lot less pressure when you're away," Hull explained. "We get big crowds both places, but obviously it's a little more pressure over here when it's a home Solheim Cup!"

Only Carlota Ciganda has as many Solheim Cup appearances as Hull, on either team, with the Spaniard keen to see Nordqvist follow calling time on her LPGA Tour playing career by leading Europe to victory.

"I would love to win for her [Nordqvist], especially now after announcing her retirement," Ciganda revealed. "I think it would be a very nice present for her.

"Not that she needs it, because she's won everything! She's been a part of so many Solheim Cups and wins. She's made so many great putts, won majors and she's done everything. I think it would be just special.

"I think she's prepared really hard, she's done her job and she's ready. Hopefully we can deliver for her."

Sky Sports Golf will have at least 12 hours of live coverage from the first two days, with coverage getting under way at 6am on Friday and Saturday ahead of the opening foursomes match teeing off at 6.40am (7.40am local time).

The afternoon fourballs are scheduled to start at 12.05pm (1.05pm local time) on both days, with coverage continuing until after the final putt is holed, while Sunday singles coverage begins at 9am ahead of the opening tee shot at 10.10am.

Sky Sports+ will have live coverage of the closing ceremony from 5.30pm on Sunday, following the Solheim Cup winner being crowned, while the opening ceremony on Thursday at 4.30pm will see the opening-day pairings revealed.

articles.title: Irish Open: Rory McIlroy four off lead in tough conditions with Shane Lowry two off top
articles.summary: In tough conditions at the Irish Open in Doonbeg, Rory McIlroy finishes opening round four shots off leader Joaquin Niemann; Ireland's Shane Lowry sits two shots off lead; Watch continued coverage of Irish Open on Friday at 9.30am and 5pm on Sky Sports+
articles.body:
Gusts up to 35mph saw balls oscillating on greens with Frenchman Frederic Lacroix seeing his blown off the putting surface at the 13th, but he had fortunately already marked so was able to replace it.

All of which made for slow going at Trump International Golf Links and Hotel in Doonbeg during Thursday's first round. As the day wore on, a course-record 65 from Chilean Joaquin Niemann looked increasingly good.

Having reached the turn at two under, Niemann had four successive birdies from the 14th to put him in contention for a $30,000 (£22,000) bonus for the lowest round of the week.

Austrian Maximilian Steinlechner and Renato Paratore appeared set to make a challenge for the top of the leaderboard at three under through 12 and 11 respectively, but could be thwarted by the fading light.

Home favourite Lowry, who won the event as a 22-year-old amateur in Baltray, kept himself in the mix, also in the clubhouse at three under.

Long waits on many tee boxes had been commonplace but McIlroy, who had won the event at the K Club last year, started with two birdies in his first four holes before getting to the turn in a two-under 34 - in three and a half hours.

After missing a four-foot birdie chance at the first he holed a 14-footer at the second, splashed out of a bunker to three feet at the par-five fourth for his second birdie, but missed from 10 feet at the seventh for a third.

McIlroy found the fairway bunker on the 13th, and a missed 10-foot putt saw him take a double-bogey hit before a fine approach to the 15th helped quickly pull a stroke back.

The world No 2, though, could not make the most of what proved limited opportunities over the closing run, narrowly missing a lengthy birdie attempt on the 18th, and will return on Friday morning hoping to improve along with the weather forecast.

McIlroy: A tough day to play in - I hung in there

"There was a couple of things that were tough today. Obviously the wind and the strength of the wind was one thing, and then the pace of play," McIlroy said.

"This course isn't conducive to sort of letting you get in a flow. Especially the first two days with so many people in the field, there is a lot of stopping and starting.

"It's hard when you are playing a round of golf and it takes six hours, it's hard to get into the rhythm of things, but felt like I did a good job.

"After making the double bogey on 13, I was just trying to get those two shots back by the end of the day. Didn't quite do that, but finishing under par for the day was a reasonable effort.

"I hung in there, shot under par, and at least don't feel like I'm out of the tournament. A good day tomorrow gets me right back in it."

Northern Ireland's Tom McKibbin - in a group with European team captain Luke Donald and Alex Fitzpatrick - finished at two under, having made a bogey on the final hole.

McIlroy was playing alongside Ryder Cup team-mate Robert MacIntyre, who finished at two over having followed a fine 37-foot birdie at 17 with a poor tee shot at the last into the deep rough before making a six.

Brooks Koepka, who received a tournament invite, endured a tough day, which started with a seven on the first and ended at five over.

Jon Rahm - linked with a return to the PGA Tour following doubts over the future of LIV Golf - was level par.
